result.title: Relation Before Action: Explicit Relation Modeling for Latent Action Pretraining
result.summary: Learning latent actions from unlabeled video sequences offers a promising way to acquire reusable action representations without relying on embodiment-specific control annotations. However, existing latent-action pretraining approaches commonly couple the modeling of visual transitions with action inference, directly mapping paired observations or derived transition cues into latent action codes. This formulation leaves two distinct tasks entangled: characterizing the relational structure of an observed transition and abstracting it into a compact action representation. We propose RELACT, a relation-first framework that explicitly separates transition relation modeling from predictive action abstraction. RELACT first constructs a structured relation representation $R$ that captures how visual elements and their interactions evolve across observations. It then infers a compact, state-conditioned stochastic latent action $U$, whose predictive effects are learned through action-conditioned latent dynamics. The resulting action representation can be grounded in native control spaces for model-based planning or used to supervise downstream embodied policies. Extensive experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain image-goal navigation, goal-conditioned manipulation, and downstream policy adaptation demonstrate improved predictive action representations and consistent gains in planning and control, supporting the effectiveness and generality of relation-first latent action pretraining.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RELACT 框架，将「转变关系建模」与「动作抽象」显式分离：先构造刻画视觉元素及其交互随观测演变的结构化关系表示 R，再推断紧凑、状态条件的随机隐动作 U，并通过动作条件的隐动力学学习其预测效果，用于规划与下游策略监督。
AI.relevance_reason: 「先显式建模关系、再压缩为紧凑 latent」的两段式设计，可能为 LVR 中视觉关系细节保留与信息坍缩之间的取舍提供核查线索，其以隐动力学预测作监督的思路也可作为 latent 状态训练信号参考；但原文目标是具身隐动作而非推理状态，迁移性需人工判断。
